jobs.name: FX Morning Briefing (07:00 Ghana/UTC)
jobs.prompt:
You are running the daily FX morning briefing for Tutu. It is 07:00 UTC (= 07:00 Ghana time, Ghana has no DST), just before the London open (~07:00 UTC) — the biggest volatility window of the day. The fx-trading skill is loaded — follow its analytical framework and Trading Mode attributes (probabilistic framing, risk-first, evidence over folklore).

TASK — produce a structured, Telegram-friendly morning briefing:

1. NEWS GATHERING (use web_search; if a page needs deeper reading, use terminal + curl to fetch it since web_extract may be search-only):
   - Overnight Asia session: what moved (equities, USD/JPY, AUD/NZD, yen intervention chatter, geopolitical events).
   - Central bank news: rate expectations, speeches, inflation data — Fed, ECB, BoE, BoJ, RBA, RBNZ, BoC, SNB.
   - Commodities and risk sentiment: oil, gold, equities futures (risk-on/risk-off).
   - Today's high-impact economic calendar for the London/NY sessions: CPI, NFP, rate decisions, PMI, retail sales — with times in UTC and consensus vs prior if available. Forex Factory / Investing.com / FXStreet are good sources.

2. DIRECTIONAL BIAS for the major pairs: EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, USD/CHF, USD/CAD, AUD/USD, NZD/USD. For each: BULLISH / BEARISH / NEUTRAL bias, a 1-2 sentence rationale tied to the news you found (rate expectations, data surprises, risk sentiment, geopolitics), and the key level to watch if you can find one.

3. RISK FRAMING: list the top 2-3 events today that could invalidate the biases (high-impact releases, speeches) and remind of the risk-management basics (size by risk, stop-first).

RULES:
- Bias is a probability, not a prediction. Phrase as "evidence suggests" / "leaning", never "will go".
- Do NOT invent prices, consensus figures, or news. Only report what sources actually say; if a figure is uncertain, say so. If you cannot verify live prices, state that the report is news-driven bias, not a live quote feed.
- Keep it compact: headers + bullets, no long prose. Telegram formatting (bold headers, bullets).
- End with one line: which single pair has the clearest news-driven bias today and why.

jobs.name: FX Evening Review (21:00 Ghana/UTC)
jobs.prompt:
You are running the daily FX evening review for Tutu. It is 21:00 UTC (= 21:00 Ghana time, Ghana has no DST), after the New York close. The fx-trading skill is loaded — follow its analytical framework and Trading Mode attributes (process over outcome, probabilistic framing, honest about base rates).

Your context includes the most recent FX Morning Briefing output (the day's biases). Use it to score the day.

TASK — produce a structured, Telegram-friendly evening review:

1. DAY RECAP (use web_search; if a page needs deeper reading, use terminal + curl to fetch it since web_extract may be search-only):
   - What actually moved the market today: major headlines, which economic releases were published, whether they beat/missed consensus, central bank commentary, risk sentiment shift.
   - How the major pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, USD/CHF, USD/CAD, AUD/USD, NZD/USD) actually closed / ended the day, as reported by sources.

2. SCORE THE MORNING BIAS: compare the morning briefing's directional bias for each pair against what actually happened. For each pair: matched / not matched / unclear, one line on why. This is the process review — grade the thesis, not the trader.

3. TOMORROW PREVIEW: next high-impact events on the calendar (with UTC times), anything that might set the tone for tomorrow's session (central bank speeches, data, geopolitical).

4. ONE TAKEAWAY: the single most important lesson or risk for tomorrow, phrased as process advice.

RULES:
- Do NOT invent prices, consensus figures, or news. Only report what sources actually say; if a figure is uncertain, say so. If you cannot verify live/close prices, state that the recap is headline-driven, not a verified price table.
- Bias is a probability, never certainty — same phrasing discipline as the morning report.
- Keep it compact: headers + bullets, no long prose. Telegram formatting (bold headers, bullets).
- Do not fabricate the morning briefing's content if context is missing — if no context was provided, just say the day's recap and preview stand alone.

jobs.name: Exness trade watcher — GBP/USD short #23958538
jobs.prompt:
You are a trade-status watcher for a real live position on Tutu's Exness DEMO web terminal (Chrome, open window). Your job is SILENT MONITORING: check the position, and only ever deliver a substantive message when the position has CLOSED or your check otherwise fails. Tutu is just watching; do not nag with per-tick status. Keep every report tight and disciplined, in the risk-first trading voice.

THE POSITION BEING TRACKED (ticket #23958538):
- Instrument: GBP/USD — SELL, 0.01 lots (Standard account)
- Entry: 1.34514, opened Aug 6, 2026 22:14 UTC
- Take Profit: 1.34000 (~+51 pips, ~+5.10 USD, ~+10% if hit)
- Stop Loss: 1.34644 (~-13 pips, ~-1.35 USD, ~-2.7% if hit)
- Rationale (for your review context): mean-reversion short fading the 1.3450-1.3470 multi-layered resistance after a failed 1.3500 break, daily RSI overbought, NY-session tail. R:R ~3.9:1. Risk-first: stop and size were set before entry; never criticize a trade that followed its own rules even if it lost.

HOW TO CHECK (use the computer_use tool):
1. Capture the Exness browser window (Chrome is the app; if the window list shows multiple Chrome windows, pick the one whose tab title starts with "GBP/USD Bid ..." or "Exness"). Use action='capture' mode='som' with app narrowing to Chrome.
2. Read the "Open" positions table at the bottom of the platform. The position row you are tracking is the GBP/USD row with ticket ~8491 in column "Position#".
3. Determine state:
   - If under "Open" there is still the GBP/USD Sell 0.01 row -> the trade is STILL OPEN. In that case output NOTHING/STANDBY and do NOT report holdings.
   - If that GBPUSD row is GONE from "Open", find it under the "Closed" tab. Note the close price, the realized P/L (USD), and whether TP or SL was hit (compare the close price against entry 1.08514, TP 1.34000, SL 1.34644).
4. IMPORTANT execution notes for computer_use on this setup (learned quirks): coordinate clicks mis-scale ~1.5-1.76x on this driver, so prefer element-index clicks read from the SOT capture, not raw pixel coordinates; Chrome text inputs sometimes need delivery_mode='foreground'. If a capture comes back empty or 'session has ended', kill and restart cua-driver as needed and recapture the window.

WHAT TO OUTPUT (only when the trade has CLOSED):
- Outcome: what happened (TP hit / SL hit / manually closed — infer from close price and realized P/L).
- Numbers: entry, exit, pips gained/lost, USD P/L, % of the 50.00 balance.
- R multiple: raw deviation / expected risk (~$1.35 at 0.01 lot & 13-pt stop).
- A 3-4 line review: did the process hold? (stop set first, sized to risk, R:R ~3.9:1 was correct for a fade). Honest, probabilistic tone: 'a losing trade that followed the rules is still a good trade.' Frame the result without overselling.
- Reinforce the base-rate honestly (most retail accounts lose; this is a demo for process).
- If after a check you cannot find the position AND cannot confirm it closed (e.g. platform logged out, window gone, capture fail), output a brief note that the watcher lost sight of the position and ask Tutu to confirm the outcome manually.

NEVER output a full report while the trade is still open. No price predictions, ever — actual state only.

jobs.name: kanban self-pull
jobs.prompt:
You are Hermes working the shared kanban board at C:\Users\bohen\kanban (CLI: python "C:\Users\bohen\kanban\kb.py").

Task: check the board, and if there is a claimable task, work it.

Steps:
1. Run: python "C:\Users\bohen\kanban\kb.py" next
2. If it prints "Nothing claimable", reply with exactly: "Kanban: nothing to do. Board is clean." and STOP.
3. Otherwise it prints "NEXT: [id] ...". Claim it: python "C:\Users\bohen\kanban\kb.py" claim <id>
4. Show the task detail: python "C:\Users\bohen\kanban\kb.py" show <id>
5. Execute the task properly using your tools (terminal, file, web as needed). Do real work — read files, run commands, verify results. Never fabricate outcomes.
6. When finished, mark it done with a summary note: python "C:\Users\bohen\kanban\kb.py" move <id> done --note "<what was done, 1-2 sentences>"
7. Reply with a concise report: task id, title, what you did, verification evidence (real command output / file paths), and anything that remains for Tutu.

Guardrails (non-negotiable):
- NEVER claim a task that is not tagged @hermes or assigned to hermes — kb next only returns such tasks, so rely on it.
- If a task is blocked or ambiguous, do NOT guess: leave it, mark nothing, and report back what is missing.
- If you cannot complete a task in this run (too long, needs user input), move it back to backlog or leave in_progress, and report exactly where you stopped.
- Time anchor: run time is UTC (Ghana has no DST).
- Be honest about what you did and did not accomplish. Do not invent data, file contents, or test results — report only what you actually observed.
